newsitem.title: ALBANIA: FORECAST - Albania expects double digit 1997 growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Albania expects double digit 1997 growth.

text.p: President Sali Berisha said on Wednesday Albania would achieve double-digit economic growth next year while striving to reduce inflation and cutting the budget deficit.
"I am optimistic that Albania will have double-digit economic growth and a single-digit inflation next year," Berisha told a news conference.
He estimated economic growth in 1996 equalled or exceeded the previous year's growth.
Albania had expected economic growth of 10 percent in 1996, compared with 13.4 percent in 1995. Berisha said the expansion of the Albanian economy was outstripping former east bloc countries.
Berisha said he would ask the government to take steps to rein in the budget deficit and blamed the current gap on inefficient tax collection.
Albania's budget deficit in October was 10.0 percent of gross domestic product, according to the Bank of Albania.
Berisha traced annual inflation of 17.4 percent to value added tax and the liberalisation of bread and fuel prices. Salaries had also risen by 30 percent, he noted.
He praised the government for implementing economic reforms in 1996 but urged it to cooperate with trade unions in indexing wages to inflation.

The president said the government would institute checks on so-called pyramid schemes, which offer big returns on short-term deposits. He also called on Albanians to deposit their money at state-owned banks.
He added that the government had compiled a strategy to privatise big sectors of the economy and would start the programme soon.
